question: Should maintainers accept the inherited focused runner/Codex regression proof for this bot replacement after conflict resolution, or require live wedged Codex app-server or WhatsApp proof before merge?
rationale: The code path is source-reproducible and covered by focused tests, but the remaining proof gap is a maintainer call because live Codex/WhatsApp wedge proof is expensive and the PR changes session lane release timing.

options.title: Resolve Conflicts And Accept Focused Proof
options.body: Adapt the PR to current main, preserve the regression coverage, and treat the focused runner/Codex proof as sufficient for this lane-release bug.

options.title: Require Live Wedge Proof
options.body: Pause merge until a live or Crabbox scenario demonstrates that a wedged Codex app-server cleanup releases the lane without corrupting later session delivery.

options.title: Pause Or Close The Replacement
options.body: Keep the PR paused or close it if maintainers decide the conflict resolution and live-proof cost is not worth this replacement branch.

recommendation.title: Resolve Conflicts And Accept Focused Proof
recommendation.body: Adapt the PR to current main, preserve the regression coverage, and treat the focused runner/Codex proof as sufficient for this lane-release bug.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the newest current-main changes on the conflicting runner/Codex surfaces and is best placed to decide the proof bar for adapting this replacement.
